neighbours.label: the adjective in 'on the bright/plus/flip side' (the other-hand idiom)
fire: The trip was expensive, but on the bright side, the weather was perfect.
This phone is heavy, though on the plus side the battery lasts for days.
Rents went up, yet on the flip side wages also rose.
We lost the match, but look on the bright side: nobody got hurt.
My new job is far away; on the plus side, the pay is better.
Taxes will fall, and on the flip side, services may shrink.
Traffic was awful, but on the bright side we heard the whole album.
The film runs long, although on the plus side the cast is superb.
quiet: The trip was expensive, and the bright sun made the beach too hot.
This phone is heavy, so a plus sign appears on the left of the screen.
Rents went up, so we had to flip the mattress and sell the bed.
We lost the match, then walked along the side of the bright canal.
My new job is far away, and each salary has a plus for overtime.
Taxes will fall, and cooks will flip burgers on the side of the road.
Traffic was awful, and bright headlights came from the other side.
The film runs long, although the side door stays open for smokers.
